title: fix(metadata-protocol): a seed resolves a lookup another package adds through objectExtensions to the target's id
body:
Fixes #35254

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：应用作者在模块里给别的包的对象加的关联字段，演示数据现在能正确连上目标记录；以前在本地开发和正式部署启动时，这类字段里存的是目标的名称文字，记录页上显示“受限记录”。
- 为什么做：模块扩展对象是垂直模块的标准做法，两个下游应用的演示数据因此连错，其中一个连带算错了客户评级和订单利润判断。
- 出错会怎样：只影响种子数据读取对象定义的方式；万一有问题，表现为某个演示数据的关联没连上或启动日志报出无法解析的引用，撤回本次改动即恢复原样。以前已存成文字的记录不会被自动改写，重新跑一次种子数据即可修正。
- 要你做什么：无

## What changes

`SeedLoaderService.resolveObjectDefinition` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`) is the one place the seed loader reads an object definition. Every per-field decision of a load goes through it: the reference graph, natural-key resolution, required-on-insert, the tenant column, the roll-up strip, the replay comparands and the undeclared-column warning.

- **Before:** it took the metadata service's copy whenever that copy had `fields`, and fell back to the engine's schema only when the metadata service had none. A boot that loads a compiled artifact (`os dev`, `os serve`, the cloud runtime) gives the metadata service each object as its own package wrote it. The fields another package adds through `objectExtensions` (ADR-0130 D5) live only in the ObjectQL registry's fold. So a lookup that an extension adds was never a reference. It had no graph edge, and its natural key was written verbatim into the foreign-key column.
- **After:** it reads the engine's registered schema first. That is the object as served, with extensions folded in. It falls back to the metadata service's copy only when the engine has no schema for the name, or exposes no schema registry (`IDataEngine` does not require one). The loader merges no extension itself: the registry's fold is the one source. The marketplace case the old fallback existed for (an object only the engine registry knows) is still served: it is now found on the first read.
- The #35655 roll-up strip (PR #36118) used to take the union of the resolved definition and `engineSchemaOf`. The resolved definition now IS the engine's schema whenever the engine has one, so the union collapses to `summaryFieldNames(objectDefinition)`. Its pins are unchanged and green.
- Docblocks that named the old order are corrected: `resolveObjectDefinition`, `seedReferenceGraphFields`, `declaresNameColumn`, and the #35655 extension pin's header in `seed-loader-summary-stale.test.ts`.
- `.changeset/35254-seed-extension-lookup.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch.

The in-process boot (`@objectstack/verify` without an artifact) bridges the metadata service from the folded registry, so the metadata copy and the engine copy already agreed there. This change makes the artifact boot read what that boot already read.

## Tests

New pins in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`, as a top-level `describe('[#35254] …')` on that file's engine double, which is already pinned. The metadata double serves the authored `ext_order` without `quote_ref`. The engine double's `getSchema` serves the folded object with `quote_ref → ext_quote`. Every case has a CONTROL: `account_ref`, a lookup the owner authored on the same object.

- `upsert` and `ignore` (the inserting modes; `insert` itself is a retired `SeedMode`): `quote_ref` stores the quote's id. `insertOrder` puts `ext_quote` (and `ext_account`) before `ext_order`. The `ext_order` node's `dependsOn` is `[ext_account, ext_quote]`, and its references include `quote_ref->ext_quote` beside `account_ref->ext_account`.
- `update`: the existing order row gets the quote's id and the account's id, and no second order is inserted.
- A cycle (`ext_quote.order_ref` back to the order): the cycle is detected, one side waits for pass 2, and both links resolve. The pass-2 writes and the `insertOrder` are identical to the CONTROL, where `quote_ref` is authored.
- An unknown natural key: both the extension lookup and the authored lookup are refused the same way (one errored record, the same error with the field and target names normalised, no raw key stored), and the extension's error names `ext_order.quote_ref`.
- `falls back to the metadata service definition when the engine has no schema for the object` (renamed from `prefers the metadata service definition …`): the engine is asked first for every seeded object, and the metadata service is read for each.

<details>
<summary>Premise on the real boot path: os dev on a two-package artifact</summary>

A fixture of the card's shape, not committed: app package `qx_app` owns `qx_account` and `qx_order` (with the authored `account_ref`). Module `qx_mod` (built with `artifactObjects`) owns `qx_quote`, adds `quote_ref` (→ `qx_quote`) to `qx_order`, seeds `O-1` in `update` mode and inserts `O-2` in `upsert` mode, both with `quote_ref` by the quote's name. The `os dev --fresh` boot came from this branch's CLI closure build, and the rows were read with `GET /api/v1/data/qx_order` as the seeded dev admin.

| leg | `O-1.quote_ref` (update) | `O-2.quote_ref` (upsert) | `account_ref` (CONTROL) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| origin/main resolver put back (blob 2713d6f4cb) | `"Acme Annual Renewal Quote"` | `"Acme Annual Renewal Quote"` | the account's id |
| this branch (blob fdbca4a779) | the quote's id | the quote's id | the account's id |

`[SeedLoader] Dependency graph built` read `insertOrder: [qx_account, qx_quote, qx_order]` on both legs. That reading does not tell the legs apart on this fixture; the unit pins assert the edge itself.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Ablation of the resolver order</summary>

The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --hold` replaced the three-line engine-first body with `origin/main`'s metadata-first body: anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1, blob fdbca4a77946 → 2713d6f4cbe4. Then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol build` ran, and `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/metadata-protocol 'fromMetadata?.fields'` read the marker present in `dist/`.

- Unit pins (source import): `Tests 7 failed | 15 passed (22)`. All five #35254 pins were red (for example `expected 'Q-ACME' to be 'gen-1'`). So were the renamed fallback pin (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'crm_account', … ]`, metadata read first) and the #35655 extension roll-up pin (`expected [ 'name', 'total', 'ext_refunds' ] to not include 'ext_refunds'`, because the union is gone). The throwing-schema CONTROL stayed green.
- `os dev` on that build: the raw names in the table above.
- Restore: `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH` in a trap. Blob after restore fdbca4a77946 equals the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and `git status --porcelain -- packages/` is empty. After a rebuild, the `--absent` dist reading passed. The tree reading reported only the uncommitted `os dev` fixture (since deleted). Green again: `Tests 22 passed (22)`, and `os dev` stored the ids.

The pins were later moved from a new file into `seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts` unchanged (see Acceptance notes). `seed-loader.ts` did not change after the ablation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Suite and gate readings</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` at e3d33403a2: `Test Files 363 passed | 9 skipped (372)`, `Tests 23325 passed | 45 skipped (23370)`. `typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0. At the head (dd697760d1, a test-file move only), the two edited test files read `Tests 22 passed (22)` and `typecheck` exits 0.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 67 families, and the list is identical at the head. All 67 ran locally, with each exit captured before any pipe:
  - 65 exited 0.
  - `check:engine-double-contract` exited 1 at e3d33403a2 (RETAINED: the new file's pinned double was not in the pinned ledger). The pins moved onto the file's already-pinned double, and the gate exits 0 at dd697760d1.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: no local `dist/` for packages outside this diff). NOT MEASURED locally; CI runs it.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", exit 0.
- `overlap-check` at dd697760d1: VERDICT clean, exit 0.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The pins live in an existing file.** The dispatch asked for a new file named after the card, unless `check:engine-double-contract` refused a new engine double. The gate asked for its pinned ledger to be regenerated (`--write`), and that ledger write was refused in this session. So the pins were folded into `seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`, whose engine double is already pinned and is the same double the new file had copied.
- **The test harness boot does not reproduce the defect.** It was measured: a dogfood test booting `bootStack` from `@objectstack/verify` with `MetadataPlugin({ artifactSource })` over the same two-package artifact read the extension field absent from `metadata.getObject('qa_ext_order')` and present in `getSchema`. Yet it stored the quote's id on BOTH legs of the ablation, so it could not pin this defect, and it is not committed. Only the real `os dev` boot showed the raw key. Why the harness's seed load sees a different definition was not established. This is reported as a finding, not fixed here. Carried by #36274.
- Rows an earlier load stored with the raw key are not rewritten. Re-running the seed in `update` or `upsert` mode replaces the key with the id (the replay compare sees a difference). The changeset says so.
- The basic-insert fallback seeder in `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` (no metadata service, or the loader threw) does not go through this resolver, as #36118's notes already record.

## Verification

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`. Expect `Tests 8 passed`, including five `[#35254]` cases.

Read first, by risk:
1. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`, the `resolveObjectDefinition` hunk: the order flip that every per-field read inherits.
2. The same file, the `summaryFields` hunk in `loadDataset`: #36118's union collapsed onto the single source.
3. `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-engine-schema-fallback.test.ts`: the probe assertion of the renamed fallback pin, and the new `[#35254]` block.
